stances.reasoning: Pledged to repeal the February 2025 citywide four-plus-two upzoning, calling it something that 'makes absolutely no sense.' Advocates density near transit corridors only, not citywide by-right multifamily — reflecting modest density with design review and strong neighborhood input.

Opposed citywide upzoning and advocates managed, transit-corridor-focused growth with financial incentives rather than blanket deregulation. His approach favors growth only where infrastructure supports it rather than streamlined permitting across the board.

Supports bike lanes 'in some cases' but has expressed parking concerns and was not endorsed by Cambridge Bicycle Safety; did not commit to completing the Cycling Safety Ordinance. Reflects a maintain-roads-while-selectively-adding-transit position rather than a transit-first approach.

Proposed a youth violence prevention program (ages 16–24) integrating Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to reduce incarceration — adding crisis-response capacity alongside existing police rather than redirecting the police budget. Reflects current funding plus crisis response teams.

Advocates financial incentives for office-to-residential conversion and transit-corridor-focused housing development — targeted subsidies and easier permitting in specific areas rather than either direct public housing construction or purely market-driven supply.
